description: ANALOX is a team exploring how science and technology can support planetary exploration. Our interests include software development, geospatial technology, data analysis, and scientific research. We're looking for curious, collaborative people with skills in Python, GIS, biology, bioinformatics, data science or planetary science. You don't need to know everything; —just be willing to learn and contribute!
summary:
ANALOX is a planetary research platform designed to help researchers discover and evaluate locations on Earth that share relevant characteristics with environments on the Moon and Mars. The project addresses the challenge of identifying terrestrial analog environments that can support planetary research, scientific investigation, and preparation for future space exploration.

Our focus is on Africa, where geological formations and extreme environments offer valuable opportunities for research but may be underrepresented in planetary analog discovery. ANALOX is designed to bring together geological information, satellite observations, terrain data, environmental measurements, and planetary datasets to help researchers identify and compare potential analog locations.

By making these locations and their supporting scientific information easier to explore, ANALOX aims to improve access to research opportunities and bring greater visibility to African environments in planetary science.
details: ANALOX is a planetary terrestrial analog discovery platform for finding Earth locations that share characteristics with the Moon or Mars — focused on African sites. WHAT IT DOES A researcher picks a planetary target (Mars or Moon) and defines research areas (Geochemistry, Climate, Mineralogy). ANALOX then: • Discovers candidate Earth sites — by scanning a lat/lon grid across Africa via NASA POWER, or by entering any coordinate on Earth • Fetches real satellite-derived climatology from NASA POWER for each candidate • Compares candidates against NASA Fact Sheet reference values using a multi-perspective consensus engine (min-max scaling → L2 distance per area → weighted sum) • Returns a decomposable ranking — total score plus per-area and per-criterion breakdown • Displays candidates on an interactive map with full source traceability • Generates reports from human-reviewed findings only HOW IT WORKS FastAPI + SQLAlchemy async + PostgreSQL 18 with pgvector + Alembic. 14-table schema: workspaces → projects → areas → criteria → candidates → characteristics → sources → findings → reports. Every measurement has a NOT NULL source_id — nothing enters without provenance. The consensus engine ports a numeric-vector similarity approach: build an N-dimensional vector from criteria, min-max scale to [0,1], compute L2 distance to the reference, aggregate per-area. Weights are per-query, never stored. No consensus_score column — similarity is computed at read time. SCIENTIFIC INTEGRITY The differentiator is the refusal to rank as truth: • Similarity is a retrieval signal, not a conclusion — no stored scores • Findings require an author and a draft → reviewed transition — the system cannot auto-confirm an analog • Sample data is labeled in the data model (is_mock column), and reports print a warning automatically • Missing data is a state, not a zero — NULL is first-class • Provenance survives every transform — sources stored verbatim IMPACT NASA's analog research needs terrestrial test sites, but candidates are scattered across datasets with no unified tool. ANALOX demonstrates a live pipeline: real NASA data in, decomposed consensus out, human-reviewed reports with provenance. The schema is dataset-agnostic — when the official challenge dataset is released, one ingestion adapter converts it into the same schema. TECHNOLOGIES Python, FastAPI, Pydantic v2, SQLAlchemy 2.0 async, asyncpg, PostgreSQL 18, pgvector, Alembic, Docker, httpx, Leaflet, pytest. DATA SOURCES • NASA POWER (NASA Langley) — https://power.larc.nasa.gov/ • NASA Mars Fact Sheet — https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/marsfact.html • NASA Moon Fact Sheet — https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/moonfact.html
